chapters.title: Chapter 2: Before You File: Documents and Pre-Checks

lessons.title: Form 16, Form 26AS and AIS: Reading Your Tax Documents

body.text: Three documents, three authors. Form 16 is your employer's version of your year. Form 26AS is the department's ledger of tax credited to your PAN. AIS is everything the department knows about your money. File only when all three agree with each other and with you.

children.text: The e-filing portal pre-fills much of your ITR from these documents. That is convenient, and dangerous. If the pre-filled data is wrong or incomplete and you accept it blindly, you file a wrong return. If you ignore it and file something that does not match, the department's systems flag the mismatch. Either way, the fix is the same: learn to read all three and reconcile them before you file.

markDefs.definition: Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number. A 10-character number every employer or other deductor must hold to deduct and deposit TDS. It appears in Part A of Form 16.

children.text: Form 16 is the TDS certificate on salary, issued under Section 395 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 203 of the Income-tax Act, 1961). Every employer that deducted TDS from your salary must give it to you by 15 June following the year. It has two parts. Part A is generated from the department's TRACES system and carries your employer's
and the tax actually deposited each quarter. Part B is prepared by your employer and shows how your salary turned into taxable income.

body.text: Form 16 is a reference document, not the final word. You do not upload it with your return. If you forgot to declare an eligible deduction to HR in the old regime, such as an 80D premium paid for your parents, you can still claim it in your ITR. The return is where your tax is finally settled, not the payroll system.

body.title: Two Jobs, Two Form 16s, One Surprise
body.scenario: Karan worked at Tech Mahindra in Pune from April to September 2025, earning ₹7,00,000, and then at Persistent Systems from October 2025 to March 2026, earning ₹8,00,000. He is in the new regime and did not tell his second employer about his earlier salary. He receives two Form 16s. Both show nil TDS. He assumes he owes nothing.
body.prompt: Why did neither employer deduct TDS, and what will Karan find when he files?
body.modelAnswer: Each employer computed tax only on the salary it paid. Tech Mahindra saw ₹7,00,000, less the ₹75,000 standard deduction, which is ₹6,25,000. Persistent saw ₹8,00,000 less ₹75,000, which is ₹7,25,000. Both are within the ₹12 lakh rebate limit, so each deducted nil. But the ITR combines both salaries, and the standard deduction is allowed only once. Total salary of ₹15,00,000 less ₹75,000 gives ₹14,25,000, which is above ₹12 lakh, so there is no rebate. Tax on slabs: 5% on ₹4 lakh is ₹20,000, 10% on ₹4 lakh is ₹40,000, and 15% on ₹2,25,000 is ₹33,750, a total of ₹93,750. Adding 4% cess of ₹3,750, he owes ₹97,500. He must pay this as self-assessment tax before filing, plus any interest for not paying advance tax. Next time, he should declare his previous salary to the new employer so TDS is deducted correctly through the year.

children.text: Form 26AS is built from the quarterly TDS and TCS returns that deductors file against your PAN: your employer, your bank, your tenant, the company paying you dividends. It is the department's record of how much tax has actually reached the government in your name. The rule is simple: you can claim credit only for TDS that appears in Form 26AS. TDS deducted from your payment but never deposited, or deposited against the wrong PAN, will not show here, and you cannot claim it until the deductor fixes it.

body.text: If TDS was cut from your salary or FD interest but does not appear in Form 26AS, do not claim it anyway and hope for the best. The department will disallow the credit and raise a demand. Contact the deductor, share your PAN, and ask them to file a correction statement. Once it reflects in 26AS, claim it.

children.text: AIS and TIS: Everything the Department Knows

markDefs.definition: Annual Information Statement. A detailed record of your financial information reported to the Income Tax Department by banks, companies, mutual funds, registrars, brokers and others, available on the e-filing portal.

Taxpayer Information Summary. A category-wise summary of your AIS, showing a processed value and a derived value that accounts for the feedback you have submitted. This is what the portal uses to pre-fill your return.
Statement of Financial Transactions. Reports that banks, mutual funds, registrars, property registrars and others must file with the department on specified high-value transactions.

children.text: reports and other sources, it captures savings account interest on which no TDS was cut, every dividend, your share sales on NSE and BSE, mutual fund redemptions, property purchases and foreign remittances. Its companion, the
, rolls this up by category and feeds the pre-filled ITR. If your return shows less income than your AIS, expect the department to ask why.

body.title: Sale Value Is Not Income
body.question: Deepak's AIS shows 'Sale of listed equity shares: ₹5,00,000' reported by his depository. He sold Tata Steel shares he had bought for ₹4,20,000, eight months earlier. What does he report in his ITR?
options: ₹5,00,000 as income, since that is what AIS shows
A short-term capital gain of ₹80,000, computed from his cost
Nothing, because TDS was not deducted on the sale
Feedback denying the entry, since it overstates his income
body.explanation: AIS reports the gross sale value, not the gain. Deepak reports the sale value and his cost, and pays tax on the ₹80,000 short-term gain, since he held the shares for less than 12 months. The AIS entry is correct as a sale value, so denying it would be wrong. Mistaking sale value for income, or ignoring sales because no TDS was deducted, are two of the most common AIS errors.

body.title: Name the Summary
body.textWithBlank: The category-wise summary of AIS that the portal uses to pre-fill your return is called the ___.
body.explanation: TIS, the Taxpayer Information Summary, shows a processed value for each category and a derived value that reflects your feedback. That is why submitting feedback before filing matters: it changes what gets pre-filled.

children.text: Putting It Together: Reconcile Before You File

body.label: The Reconciliation Rule
body.value: Claim TDS as per 26AS. Report income as per AIS, after checking it.
body.context: Form 16 explains your salary. Form 26AS decides how much TDS credit you get. AIS tells you which income the department already knows about.

body.title: Total Your TDS Credit
body.prompt: Back to Aditi. Her Form 16 shows TDS of ₹86,320. Her Form 26AS also shows TDS of ₹6,500 deducted by ICICI Bank on FD interest of ₹65,000, and ₹1,200 deducted by ITC on a dividend of ₹12,000. Every entry in her 26AS is correct. What is the total TDS credit she should claim in her ITR?
body.explanation: ₹86,320 salary TDS + ₹6,500 FD interest TDS + ₹1,200 dividend TDS = ₹94,020. Remember the other side too: the ₹65,000 interest and ₹12,000 dividend must be added to her income under income from other sources. Claiming the TDS while leaving out the income behind it is a guaranteed mismatch.

content.caption: Download Paths on the e-Filing Portal

cells: Form 16
From your employer's HR or payroll portal. The e-filing portal does not issue it to employees
Form 26AS
Log in, go to e-File, then Income Tax Returns, then View Form 26AS. You are redirected to TRACES, where you choose the assessment year and format
AIS and TIS
Log in and select AIS from the top menu. On the AIS homepage, open the Annual Information Statement or the Taxpayer Information Summary for the financial year, and download as PDF or JSON
PDF password
Usually your PAN in lower case followed by your date of birth in DDMMYYYY format

body.title: New Form Numbers Coming Under the Income-tax Rules, 2026

cards.definition: Becomes Form 130, the TDS certificate on salary. For FY 2025-26, issued in June 2026, you will still receive Form 16.
Becomes Form 131, the TDS certificate for non-salary payments like FD interest.
Replaced by Form 168, the annual information statement under the new Rules, from Tax Year 2026-27.
Merged into a single Form 121, the declaration to receive interest without TDS when your tax is nil.
Becomes Form 125, the declaration a specified senior citizen aged 75 or above gives the bank to skip filing.

body.title: Your Pre-Filing Document Reconciliation
steps: Collect Form 16 from every employer you worked for during FY 2025-26
Check that the PAN, TAN and employment period in each Part A are correct
Download Form 26AS and match salary TDS for each employer against Part A of their Form 16
List every other TDS entry in 26AS: FD interest, dividends, rent, property sale
Download AIS and TIS and go through every category, not just TDS
Match savings interest, dividends and share or mutual fund sales against your own bank, broker and CAMS or KFintech statements
Submit feedback on any AIS entry that is wrong, duplicate or not yours
Chase any deductor whose TDS is missing from 26AS, before you file

points: Form 16, issued under Section 395 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 203 of the 1961 Act) by 15 June, has Part A with TDS deposited from TRACES and Part B with the employer's salary computation
Form 16 reflects only what you declared to your employer; with two jobs, each employer may under-deduct, and the ITR combines everything
Form 26AS is the department's TDS and TCS ledger, and you can claim credit only for TDS that appears in it
AIS captures much more, including savings interest, dividends, share and mutual fund sales and property deals, and TIS summarises it to pre-fill your return
AIS shows gross sale values, not gains, and wrong or duplicate entries should be corrected through feedback before filing
Reconcile all three from mid-June onwards, after Q4 TDS returns are processed, and remember the new Rules renumber these forms from Tax Year 2026-27

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax advice. Examples are simplified and illustrative. Form formats, portal navigation, TDS thresholds and form numbers under the Income-tax Rules, 2026 reflect the position at the time of writing and can change. Always verify with the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal or a qualified tax professional.
